card.title: Normal force
card.body: The contact force $\vec{N}$ a surface exerts **perpendicular** (normal) to itself, pushing outward to prevent an object from passing through it.
card.says: $N$ has **no single universal formula**—it adjusts to whatever value satisfies $\sum F_\perp = m a_\perp$, so $N = mg$ only on a flat floor with no other vertical forces or vertical acceleration.
card.from: microscopic electromagnetic repulsion between atoms at the contact surface; by Newton's third law, the object pushes on the surface with equal and opposite magnitude $N$.
card.useWhen: an object touches a floor, wall, table, or ramp—especially before calculating friction ($f_{s,\max} = \mu_s N$ or $f_k = \mu_k N$) or finding apparent weight in an elevator.
card.example: A $10\text{ kg}$ crate ($g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$, $W = 98\text{ N}$) rests on a flat floor while someone pushes straight down with $22\text{ N}$ → $N = 98 + 22 = 120\text{ N}$ upward.
card.analogy: A bathroom scale's spring: it compresses just enough to hold you up, and its reading is the normal force $N$, not always your true weight $mg$.
